messages.subject: n_divergent issues, and a non-central parameterisation
parts:
Hello all,

I am having some trouble with the following model. It is a model with three levels of hierarchy, and so when I worked with the central parameterisation of the form shown below, I unsurprisingly got issues with n_divergent. I then tried re-specifying the model in a non-CA form, but seem to be getting some issues whereby the Stan model throws a lot of errors, and crashes R. 

The errors I get are of the form: 'Invalid value of mu...." when I run the non-CA model. (I recognise that I am probably doing something wrong with the setting up of this model). 

It would be great to get some guidance on:

1. How to deal with the n_divergent issue. I have tried increasing adapt_delta, but the program takes prohibitively long to run.

2. Am I correctly implementing a non-CA version of the model? I recognise it is only a partly non-CA model, since I still have centralised parameters from the middle to the top hierarchy.

Best,

Ben

Original model:

data {


  int<lower=0> N; 
  int<lower=0> K;
  int Y[N];
  int S[K]; 
  vector[N] t; 
  int Pos[K]; 
  int RelFreq[K]; 
  int PosRel[K]; 
  int<lower=0> NReleases; 
  vector[NReleases] RelNumber;
  vector[NReleases] RelTime;
  int<lower=0> nStudy; 
  int StudyIndex[K];
  int<lower=0> nSpecies; 
  int SpeciesIndex[K]; 
  } 


parameters {
  real mPsi[nSpecies];
  real<lower=0> sigmaPsi[nSpecies];
  real<lower=0,upper=1> psi[K];
  real mMu[nSpecies];
  real<lower=0> sigmaMu[nSpecies];
  real<lower=0,upper=1> mu[K];
  real<lower=0,upper=1000> kappa[K];
  real p[nSpecies];
  real<lower=0> r[nSpecies];
  real a;
  real<lower=0> b;
  real c;
  real<lower=0> d;
  real e;
  real<lower=0> f;
  real g;
  real<lower=0> h;
  real q;
  real<lower=0> w;
  real v;
  real<lower=0> z;
} 

  
transformed parameters {
  real phi[K];
  real eta[K];
  for (i in 1:K)
  {
phi[i] <- logit(psi[i]);
eta[i] <- logit(mu[i]);
  }
}
 
model {
  for (i in 1:K) {
real lambda[S[i]];
int tempSpeciesIndex;
tempSpeciesIndex <- SpeciesIndex[i];
if (RelFreq[i]< 2) ## Single release
{
real R_times_psi;
R_times_psi <- RelNumber[PosRel[i]]*psi[i];
for (j in 1:S[i])
{
lambda[j]<- R_times_psi*(1 - mu[i])^t[Pos[i] + j - 1];
Y[Pos[i] + j - 1] ~ neg_binomial_2(lambda[j],kappa[i]);
}
}
else ## Multiple release
{
for (j in 1:S[i])
{
real lambdaTemp;
lambdaTemp <- 0;
for (kk in 1:RelFreq[i])
{
if (t[Pos[i] + j - 1]> RelTime[PosRel[i]+kk-1])
{
lambdaTemp <- lambdaTemp + psi[i]*RelNumber[PosRel[i] + kk - 1]*(1-mu[i])^(t[Pos[i] + j - 1] - RelTime[PosRel[i]+kk-1]);
}
}
lambda[j] <- lambdaTemp;
Y[Pos[i] + j - 1] ~ neg_binomial_2(lambda[j],kappa[i]);
}
}
  }
  ## Basic
  for (i in 1:K)
  {
   int speciesTemp;
   speciesTemp <- SpeciesIndex[i];
   eta[i] ~ normal(mMu[speciesTemp],sigmaMu[speciesTemp]);
   phi[i] ~ normal(mPsi[speciesTemp],sigmaPsi[speciesTemp]);
   kappa[i] ~ lognormal(p[speciesTemp],r[speciesTemp]);
  }
  
  mMu ~ normal(a,b);
  mPsi ~ normal(c,d);
  sigmaMu ~ cauchy(e,f);
  sigmaPsi ~ cauchy(g,h);
  p ~ normal(q,w);
  r ~ cauchy(v,z);
  
  a ~ normal(0,10);
  b ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
  c ~ normal(0,10);
  d ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
  e ~ normal(0,3);
  f ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
  g ~ normal(0,3);
  h ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
  q ~ normal(0,3);
  w ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
  v ~ normal(0,3);
  z ~ cauchy(0,2.5);

  for (i in 1:K)
  {
increment_log_prob(-log(fabs(mu[i]*(1-mu[i]))));
increment_log_prob(-log(fabs(psi[i]*(1-psi[i]))));
  }
}

I don't understand your models, but have some general
comments inline.

I'm not sure how well a Cauchy hierarchical model could
be expected to work.

Do you have a reproducible example that crashes R? And
when you say "crashes R", is that the terminal, GUI, or
RStudio?

> On Jun 18, 2015, at 12:45 PM, Ben Lambert <ben.c....@googlemail.com> wrote:
>
> Hello all,
>
> I am having some trouble with the following model. It is a model with three levels of hierarchy, and so when I worked with the central parameterisation of the form shown below, I unsurprisingly got issues with n_divergent. I then tried re-specifying the model in a non-CA form, but seem to be getting some issues whereby the Stan model throws a lot of errors, and crashes R.
>
> The errors I get are of the form: 'Invalid value of mu...." when I run the non-CA model. (I recognise that I am probably doing something wrong with the setting up of this model).

Is there a distribution function throwing that error? It helps
us a lot to see the whole output.

> It would be great to get some guidance on:
>
> 1. How to deal with the n_divergent issue. I have tried increasing adapt_delta, but the program takes prohibitively long to run.

The adapt_delta is the target acceptance rate. If you're
getting divergences during warmup, you'll also want to lower stepsize.
> 2. Am I correctly implementing a non-CA version of the model? I recognise it is only a partly non-CA model, since I still have centralised parameters from the middle to the top hierarchy.

The model's too complex to easily see what's going on.

I don't know how you're initializing, but with a constraint like:

> real<lower=0,upper=1000> kappa[K];

the random init will be centered around kappa = 500. So unless
that's a reasonable value for kapppa, this is going to be problematic
without custom inits. We generally recommend soft constraints
and positive-constrained parameters.

You shouldn't need fabs() around mu * (1 - mu) given that
mu is constrained to be in (0,1).

- Bob

Hi Bob,

Thanks for your answer. I can't think of how to come up with a similar example, (due mainly to the complexity and specific issues with the model), but I will keep thinking.

I will try using non-Cauchy hierarchical priors, to see if that helps.

Basically the three level hierarchy is because the data is a meta anaysis of individual time species (1st level), which come from different species of mosquito (2nd level). The top level is an overarching distribution across all mosquito species.

The model works fine when I just use a two level hierarchy. However, when I move to three levels, I get the aforementioned issues with n_divergent.

Best,

Ben

phi[i] <- mPsi[speciesTemp] + phi_raw[speciesTemp]*sigmaPsi[speciesTemp];
kappa[i] <- exp(p[speciesTemp] + lkappa_raw[speciesTemp]*r[speciesTemp]);
  }
  
  for (i in 1:K)
  {
psi[i] <- inv_logit(phi[i]);
mu[i] <- inv_logit(eta[i]);
  }
}
 
model {
  for (i in 1:K) {
real lambda[S[i]];
int tempSpeciesIndex;
tempSpeciesIndex <- SpeciesIndex[i];
if (RelFreq[i]< 2) ## Single release
{
real R_times_psi;
R_times_psi <- RelNumber[PosRel[i]]*psi[i];
for (j in 1:S[i])
{
lambda[j]<- R_times_psi*(1 - mu[i])^t[Pos[i] + j - 1];
Y[Pos[i] + j - 1] ~ neg_binomial_2(lambda[j],kappa[i]);
}
}
else ## Multiple release
{
for (j in 1:S[i])
{
real lambdaTemp;
lambdaTemp <- 0;
for (kk in 1:RelFreq[i])
{
if (t[Pos[i] + j - 1]> RelTime[PosRel[i]+kk-1])
{
lambdaTemp <- lambdaTemp + psi[i]*RelNumber[PosRel[i] + kk - 1]*(1-mu[i])^(t[Pos[i] + j - 1] - RelTime[PosRel[i]+kk-1]);
}
}
lambda[j] <- lambdaTemp;
Y[Pos[i] + j - 1] ~ neg_binomial_2(lambda[j],kappa[i]);
}
}
  }
  
  eta_raw ~ normal(0,1);
  phi_raw ~ normal(0,1);
  lkappa_raw ~ normal(0,1);
  
  mMu ~ normal(a,b);
  mPsi ~ normal(c,d);
  sigmaMu ~ cauchy(e,f);
  sigmaPsi ~ cauchy(g,h);
  p ~ normal(q,w);
  r ~ cauchy(v,z);
  
  a ~ normal(0,10);
  b ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
  c ~ normal(0,10);
  d ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
  e ~ normal(0,3);
  f ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
  g ~ normal(0,3);
  h ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
  q ~ normal(0,3);
  w ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
  v ~ normal(0,3);
  z ~ cauchy(0,2.5);

}

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: n_divergent issues, and a non-central parameterisation
parts:
The first thing I'd try is simulating some data to see if
you can fit that or if the errors are coming from model
misspecification.

The other issue when you get multiple levels of the hierarchy
is to make sure the model's identified and you're not introducing
multiple means/locations.

Otherwise, negative binomial is itself tricky to fit without
strong priors because it's so flexible.

- Bob
